{"design":"PLAN (2026-11-24), for Mark to approve or redirect.

WHAT §5.2 RANK 2 ASKS FOR: ACME DNS-01, because the agent is usually not
reachable on port 80 or 443 from the internet, so HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01
are out. The client is instant-acme 0.8.5, which takes any challenge type
and leaves DNS-01 to the caller. Three ways to write the TXT record: an
RFC 2136 dynamic update with a TSIG key; acme-dns, reached by a CNAME from
_acme-challenge; and a hook command the user writes.

HOW IT SPLITS, and why I would not do it in one go:

  A. THE ACME CORE. `[tls] source = "acme"` with `[tls.acme]` directory,
     contact and dns; the account key and order state in the state
     directory; the order, the DNS-01 challenge, polling, finalisation,
     the certificate into the same place `local-ca` keeps its own; renewal
     at two thirds of the lifetime through the reload loop that already
     exists. Roughly 400 to 600 lines.

  B. THE HOOK METHOD. `dns = "hook"` runs the operator's command with the
     record name and value, waits for it, and expects the record to be
     live. The smallest of the three and the one that covers everyone who
     can script their own DNS, the way lego, acme.sh and certbot's manual
     hooks do. Roughly 100 lines, and testable with a shell script that
     writes to a file.

  C. RFC 2136 WITH TSIG. This is its own piece, not a flag on A: DNS
     message encoding for UPDATE, the TSIG record, HMAC-SHA256 over the
     right canonical form, and either UDP with a TCP fallback or TCP
     throughout. Needs a fake authoritative server in the tests to be
     offline. Roughly 400 to 600 lines on its own.

  D. ACME-DNS. An HTTP POST to the acme-dns instance with its credentials,
     plus the CNAME the user sets up once by hand. Small, maybe 100 lines,
     but it needs A first.

TESTS, ALL OFFLINE. A and B want a fake ACME server in-process: the
directory, a nonce, an account, an order, a challenge and a certificate,
over axum, with the JWS taken as read rather than verified, since what is
under test is mimid's state machine and not instant-acme's signing. C
wants a fake authoritative server as well. Nothing here reaches Let's
Encrypt, and a staging directory is NOT a substitute, because a test that
needs the network is not a test this repo runs.

WHAT I PROPOSE: do A and B now, as one commit, which gives a working
automated certificate for anyone who can write a DNS hook. Then ask
whether C and D are worth their own beads, rather than filing them
unilaterally (AGENTS.md: sub-issues only when the bead is next on the
critical path, and Mark approves each plan first).

WORTH SAYING BEFORE ANY OF IT: this bead's value dropped once
`source = "local-ca"` landed (bead mimid-e13m.9). The certificate story is
now tailscale for a tailnet, files for a certificate you already have, and
local-ca for a user with neither. ACME serves the user who has a domain
AND wants it automated — but `files` plus certbot already covers that with
one cron line. So this automates what is already possible rather than
enabling anything new, and it is the largest remaining piece of
mimid-e13m. If something else is worth more, this is the one to defer.
"}

new_value: ACME DNS-01 ships with both methods that are being built: dns = "hook" (665c6092) and dns = "acme-dns" (ff18fe70), plus the account and order state in the state directory and renewal at two thirds of the certificate's own lifetime (dbff5cc3). RFC 2136 was dropped by Mark's call, recorded on mimid-e13m.8.1 and in §5.2 rank 2.
